explanations: No defect. Although the query is assembled by string concatenation, every user-supplied value reaches the database as a bound parameter (statuses, assignee, search text, limit, offset). The only parts concatenated into the SQL text are literal fragments from the code, generated placeholder names (:status0, :status1, ...), and the ORDER BY column and direction, which are chosen from the SORTABLE allowlist or a fixed ASC/DESC pair, never copied from input.

orderBy() uses TicketFilter::SORTABLE[$filter->sort] and throws InvalidArgumentException otherwise, so the SQL contains only trusted column names; the direction is normalised to ASC/DESC. No quoting or character stripping is applied, and the prepare mode does not protect identifiers.
Placeholder names are built from the loop index, not from the values, and each value is bound with bindValue. There is no enum validation in this code; safety comes from binding.

Binding already prevents injection. LIKE wildcards are still interpreted inside a bound value, so escapeLike prefixes %, _ and the escape character itself with '!' and the ESCAPE clause tells the database to treat them literally.
